item.title: Maximum Diversity and Support Transitions on Disks and Three-Dimensional Balls
item.description: arXiv:2610.38031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the similarity kernel $e^{-|x-y|}$, we determine the probability measure of maximum diversity on every planar disk and three-dimensional ball, answering a question of Leinster and Roff. In each dimension the measure is uniform on the boundary up to a threshold. Above it, the support is a closed central ball and the outer sphere, separated by a mass-free annulus. In dimensions two and three, their conjecture of finitely many supporting spheres therefore holds only up to the respective threshold. We obtain the measure explicitly up to one scalar root in three dimensions and through Fredholm integral equations and a scalar contact equation in the plane. Computations in dimensions four and five suggest that interior supporting spheres appear one at a time.
item.dc:creator: Adam Dajani

item.title: The 120-Cell Dissected by the Hyperplanes of Its Final Stellation: the golden ring Z[phi] as foundation, from Kramer's seven cells to 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits
item.description: arXiv:2610.38369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The diagonals of a regular pentagon dissect it into eleven pieces and draw a pentagram; the dodecahedron dissected by the twelve face planes of its inner core gives Kramer's seven "elementary cells" of 1982. We define the stellation dissection of a golden regular polytope in any dimension as the dissection of the convex hull of its final regular stellation by the facet hyperplanes of the core, show that the core has phi^(-d) of the inradius of the hull for d = 2, 3, 4, and carry the dissection out for the first time on the 120-cell. The foundation is the arithmetic of the golden ring Z[phi], the ring of integers of Q(sqrt 5): vertices and hyperplanes live in Z[phi]^d, every orientation test is the exact sign of an element of Z[phi], decided with integers, and the pieces are named by sign vectors. We develop this foundation from scratch (conjugation, norm, units, the primes sqrt 5, 2, 3, the exact sign test, the lattice x -> (x, conj x), the vertex modules of the dodecahedron and the 120-cell, the icosian ring) and let it carry the geometry. The definition bifurcates in dimension four: the star cut at depth phi^(-4), a unit, has 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits of H4; the hereditary cut at depth 1 - phi^(-4) = sqrt 5 / phi^2, a unit times the ramified prime, induces the three-dimensional dissection on every facet and has 8,161 cells in 8 orbits. New here: all vertices of the dodecahedral and of the hereditary dissection lie in the vertex module of the polytope being cut, whereas the star cut needs the denominators 2, 3 and 5; the seven kinds of pieces of the dodecahedron are exactly the I_h-orbits of sign vectors, with stellation layer equal to the number of plus signs. We catalogue the four-dimensional pieces and treat the circumscribed disc, ball and 4-ball. Every number quoted is recomputed exactly by a script whose output is reproduced in an appendix.
item.dc:creator: Miguel E. P\'erez Ibarra, Jaziel Flores Rodr\'iguez

item.title: Solution of Laczkovich's Lipschitz mapping problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.38834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1991, Laczkovich asked whether every measurable set of positive measure in $\mathbb R^d$ can be mapped onto a cube with a Lipschitz map. We show that the answer is positive for every $d$. Our results also give a positive answer for Kolmogorov's problem on contractions onto polygons with small measure loss in the case of Jordan measurable sets.
item.dc:creator: Attila G\'asp\'ar

item.title: The Discrete Monotonicity Property in Rank Two
item.description: arXiv:2610.39026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Betke--Henk--Wills conjecture predicts a bound for lattice-point counts in terms of successive minima. Malikiosis introduced the discrete monotonicity property for normalized residue counts as a sufficient condition for this bound and its extension to nonsymmetric convex bodies. We prove that every compact convex set satisfies this property for lattice subgroups of rank at most two, in arbitrary ambient dimension.
item.dc:creator: Fei Xue

item.title: On $\kappa$-covering minima
item.description: arXiv:2610.39034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce $\kappa$-covering minima by requiring the permutation simplices of one independent lattice frame to fit into translates of a common dilate of a convex body. We prove a lower bound for their normalized product, with coefficient $(n+1)/2^n$ for centrally symmetric bodies and an explicit dependence on Minkowski asymmetry in general. On Euclidean balls, the supremum over full-rank lattices of the ratio of the resulting fitting radius to the covering radius has order $\sqrt n$. We also establish basic comparisons with classical lattice minima and bounds under products, projections, Minkowski addition, and free direct sums. We extend the definition by allowing projected periodic lattice triangulations. These extended minima agree with the classical covering minima on ellipsoids.
item.dc:creator: Fei Xue

item.title: Borsuk number in four dimensions is at most seven
item.description: arXiv:2610.39078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every bounded set of diameter one in four-dimensional Euclidean space can be covered by seven balls of diameter strictly smaller than $0.9999$. In particular, the Borsuk number satisfies $b_4\le7$. The proof combines geometric arguments based on contact points of the circumball with an exact finite computation. For small and large circumradius, the covering centres are constructed analytically. In the remaining range, a suitable triangle of contact points reduces the problem to a four-parameter family of ball polytopes. The parameter cube is subdivided into 23494 boxes. For each parameter box, candidate centres are found by nonlinear optimization, and the resulting covering is verified using exact rational interval arithmetic and paraboloid lifting.
item.dc:creator: Andrii Arman, Andriy Bondarenko, Andriy Prymak, Danylo Radchenko

item.title: The measure contraction property and rectifiability
item.description: arXiv:2610.39083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a metric measure space $(X,d,\mathfrak{m})$ with finite upper $N$-density that satisfies $\mathsf{MCP}(K,N)$ is $N$-rectifiable. This removes a unique tangent requirement from arXiv:2505.01151.
item.dc:creator: Sean Li

item.title: Lipschitz volume rigidity for non-collapsed $\rm RCD$ spaces with boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.39493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Lipschitz-volume rigidity for non-collapsed ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces, possibly with boundary. We prove that a measure-preserving $1$-Lipschitz map between such spaces restricts to an isometry from the interior of the domain onto its image, where the latter is equipped with the intrinsic length distance. We then characterize when this interior rigidity extends to an isometric bijection between the whole spaces, in terms of the behavior of the map on the boundaries. Along the way, we establish a rigidity result of independent interest in a more general class of rectifiable metric spaces.
item.dc:creator: Zhenhao Li, Enrico Pasqualetto, Xin Qian

item.title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
item.description: arXiv:2610.39967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.
item.dc:creator: Kaiwen Yang

item.title: Integrable and non-integrable LR geodesic flows on 5-dimensional 2-step nilpotent Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.40013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate sub-Riemannian geodesic flows on 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: the Heisenberg group $H_5$ and the 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie group with a 2-dimensional commutator subgroup. For each group, we study geodesic flows associated with both left-invariant (LL) and right-invariant (LR) distributions, deriving explicit descriptions of the corresponding geodesics and comparing their integrability properties. While the LL systems are known to be Liouville integrable, and even superintegrable, we show that LR systems are Liouville integrable only in two cases: on the Heisenberg group and, for the second group, on a distinguished invariant level set.
item.dc:creator: Milan Pavlovi\'{c}, Tijana \v{S}ukilovi\'{c}

item.title: Gromov-Hausdorff versus Hausdorff distances for Euclidean submanifolds with positive reach
item.description: arXiv:2610.40286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is about comparing the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between a pair of sets to the Hausdorff distance between the pair. Recent work on this problem has focused on two settings, Riemannian manifolds and metric graphs. Here, we focus on embedded submanifolds of Euclidean space endowed with the Euclidean metric. We prove that when $\mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact connected embedded submanifold without boundary, with positive reach, and $\mathrm{A}\subset\mathcal{M}$ is a subset that is sufficiently dense in $\mathcal{M}$ with respect to the reach, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathcal{M}$ is bounded below by $1/2$ of the Hausdorff distance between them. We extend this result in two ways. First, we show that the factor $1/2$ can be improved using Jung's theorem. Second, we prove bounds on the Gromov-Hausdorff distance for pairs of subsets of $\mathcal{M}$. When $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ is equipped with the two-dimensional Euclidean metric, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ and any sufficiently dense subset of $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ can be expressed explicitly as a function of the Hausdorff distance between the two. We use interleavings between geometric simplicial complexes, nerve lemmas, properties of reach and the nearest-point projection map, and the fundamental class to produce the inequalities for general $\mathcal{M}$. We use the Borsuk-Ulam theorem for $\mathcal{M}=\mathbb{S}^1\subset \mathbb{R}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Prasanna Brahme, William Ott

item.title: A complete solution to the reverse isoperimetric problem for $\lambda$-convex bodies
item.description: arXiv:2610.40291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a given $\lambda > 0$, a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called $\lambda$-convex if it is the intersection of balls of radius $1/\lambda$. We show that among all $\lambda$-convex bodies in $\mathbb R^n$ of a given surface area, volume is minimized by the $\lambda$-convex lens, that is, the intersection of two balls of radius $1/\lambda$. This confirms a conjecture of Borisenko in all dimensions $n \geq 2$. Moreover, we extend this reverse isoperimetric inequality to all model spaces of constant curvature in arbitrary dimension and arbitrary $\lambda > 0$.
item.dc:creator: Kostiantyn Drach, Kateryna Tatarko

item.title: Almost Homogeneity Characterizes Almost Bi-Lipschitz Euclidean Embeddability
item.description: arXiv:2610.40601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A metric space admits an almost bi-Lipschitz embedding into a Euclidean space if and only if it is almost homogeneous. We prove the sufficient direction, complementing the known necessary condition. More quantitatively, we bound the target dimension and the embedding constants for every logarithmic exponent $\gamma>1$. The bounds depend only on the covering parameters in the almost homogeneity condition. In particular every doubling metric space admits such an embedding. This answers a question of Margaris and Robinson and the almost bi-Lipschitz part of a question of Olson and Robinson. As a consequence, the difference set of the image is doubling, which answers the difference-set questions of Olson and Robinson and of Margaris.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Fukano

item.title: The generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.37817v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture, including rigidity in the equality case. As a corollary, we obtain that isoperimetric regions are bounded. We prove the conjecture for Alexandrov spaces with two sided curvature bounds as well. A sharp Michael-Simon-type inequality for hypersurfaces in these spaces is also shown.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Agnoletto, M\'arcio Fabiano Da Silva, Stefano Nardulli, Reinaldo Resende

item.title: Quasiisometric embeddings of right-angled Artin groups into products
item.description: arXiv:2610.37824v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide obstructions to the existence of quasiisometric embeddings of right-angled Artin groups into products of trees, hyperbolic spaces, and other right-angled Artin groups.
item.dc:creator: Shaked Bader, Oussama Bensaid, Harry Petyt

item.title: Sobolev Inequalities Relating Rough Riemannian Metrics to their Distance Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.37884v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In previous papers, the first named author and E. Bryden explored Sobolev like inequalities relating the norm of a Riemmanian metric $g_1$, in terms of a background Riemannian metric $g_0$, in order to estimate the distance function $d_{g_1}$. Although $|g_1|_{g_0}$ is not the gradient of the distance function $d_{g_1}$, it was shown that a Morrey and Sobolev inequalities hold in their appropriate domains. In this paper we see that these results can be extended to the case where $g_1$ is a Rough Riemannian metric, something roughly analogous to an $L^{\infty}$ metric. We show that the proof of the Morrey and Sobolev inequality go through, with appropriate adjustments, as well as convergence results. We also adapt previous examples from the literature to the rough Riemannian metric case which show the hypotheses from the main theorems are necessary.
item.dc:creator: Brian Allen, Lisa Naples

item.title: Carnot geodesics with H\"older controls
item.description: arXiv:2610.38481v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an explicit length-minimizing curve in a polynomial rank-two sub-Riemannian structure on $\R^4$. Its arclength parametrization is $C^{1,1/2}$ and is not $C^{1,\alpha}$ near an interior point for any $\alpha>1/2$. Minimality is proved by an approximate calibration chosen separately for each competitor. The example admits a minimizing lift to a rank-two Carnot group of step five. Generalizations are announced.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Cavallucci, Enrico Le Donne, Sebastiano Nicolussi Golo

item.title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.38900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Kolpakov

item.title: Topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.38962v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition on length-minimizing curves in the metric tangent space. We prove that sufficiently small spheres are Lipschitz hypersurfaces homeomorphic to Euclidean spheres, while closed balls are homeomorphic to Euclidean closed balls, and open balls are diffeomorphic to Euclidean open balls. These results improve the known ones and extend them beyond two-step distributions. The proof relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for the distance, of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Luca Rizzi, Giuditta Rovelli

item.title: Large deviations for random walks generated by countable groups: a unified approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.39033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a unified treatment of various large deviation principles in the context of random walks induced by actions of countable groups. The fundamental notion undergirding the global perspective is that of weakly almost additive random walks, inspired by earlier works on the metric geometry of group actions as well as by recent developments in the theory of nonadditive thermodynamic formalism. We treat large deviations of the renormalized vector-valued distance function from the origin for groups acting simultaneously, by isometries and in a weakly almost additive fashion, on an arbitrary number of metric spaces. The foremost class of examples is provided by group actions with contracting elements, which encompasses, among others, actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and mapping class group actions on Teichm\"uller spaces. We further establish large deviation principles for quasimorphisms on countable groups, and for random walks generated by compositions of Euclidean isometries; also, we discuss extensions and streamlining of known large deviation results for singular values of random matrix products. Finally, in all the contemplated cases, we investigate the analytic properties of the rate function, leveraging its expression as the Fenchel-Legendre transform of a pressure function for certain nonadditive sequences of potentials on shift spaces.
item.dc:creator: Emilio Corso

item.title: Generalized Discrete Fractal Dimensions of Graph Families
item.description: arXiv:2610.39187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantifying the self-similarity of complex networks via discrete fractal dimensions is a fundamental problem in network science. In this paper, we investigate some general fractal dimensions of graph families based on q-energy and R\'enyi entropy. We first establish several bounds for the energy, and then discuss the monotonicity, measure invariance of the dimensions, as well as some concrete graph families.
item.dc:creator: Jiantao Liu, Cheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Qingcheng Zeng

item.title: Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps from $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces to $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.39644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a quantitative criterion for local Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps in the sense of Korevaar and Schoen from finite-dimensional \(\RCD(K,N)\) spaces into complete \(\CAT(0)\) spaces, without assuming harmonicity. We quantify the failure of local energy minimality by the harmonic replacement potential, a dyadic sum of the square roots of normalized energy gaps between a map and its harmonic replacements. We prove that this potential, together with an averaged energy term, controls the minimal weak upper gradient pointwise, with constants depending only on the curvature-dimension bounds and the scale. In particular, local boundedness of the replacement potential implies that the map admits a locally Lipschitz representative.
item.dc:creator: Bang-Xian Han, Zeyu Wang

item.title: Formalizing the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes by a Generalized Notion of Co-dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.39674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we formalize the concept of intrinsic dimension of objective landscapes introduced in Li et al. (2018), which measures the structural complexity of learning problems by training along randomly generated subspaces. We define the intrinsic dimension of a set $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^p$ as the minimal dimension $d_{\mathrm{int}}(\Theta)$ such that a random plane of dimension $d_{\mathrm{int}}(\Theta)$ in $\mathbb{R}^p$ intersects $\Theta$ with probability one. We show that it is a generalized notion of co-dimension that depends on the global geometry of $\Theta$. We study mathematical properties of the intrinsic dimension and develop techniques to estimate the intrinsic dimension of sets $\Theta$ that arise in learning problems. More specifically, we derive upper and/or lower bounds where $\Theta$ is the set of optimal parameters in student-teacher settings with shallow and deep ReLU networks, including finite and infinite sample cases, and with and without regularization. We discuss how our theory leads to novel types of generalization bounds, thereby showing that the intrinsic dimension is a measure of learning complexity. Our results connect techniques from seemingly different areas of machine learning research such as classification of symmetries of ReLU networks and stochastic geometry.
item.dc:creator: Ernesto Araya, Gitta Kutyniok, Weilin Li, Johannes Maly, Manjot Singh

item.title: Johnson optimality and uniqueness for distance ratio $1:\sqrt{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40367v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a two-distance set in $\mathbb R^d$ with distance ratio $1:\sqrt{2}$ has at most $d(d+1)/2$ points for every $d\ge9$. Equality in full affine dimension characterizes the Johnson construction; for $d\ge10$, the full-dimensional condition is automatic. The proof separates configurations according to the connectivity of the short-distance graph. The connected case uses root lattices and intersection theorems, while the disconnected case uses an orthogonal decomposition into component direction spaces and the span of their center differences. We also prove a relative bound for Euclidean two-distance sets and show that equality forces sphericity. Together with the Larman--Rogers--Seidel theorem, these results give maximum cardinality $d(d+1)/2$ for $9\le d\le21$ and $275$ for $d=22$, without exhaustive enumeration.
item.dc:creator: Bryan Bu, Chin-Yen Lee, Yu-Hang Sheng, Meng-Tsung Tsai, Hyunjun Yi, Wei-Hsuan Yu

item.title: Quasi-conformal VS quasi-isometric equivalence in spaces with controlled growth
item.description: arXiv:2510.12161v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study conditions under which quasi-conformal homeomorphisms are quasi-isometries. We show that if two nilpotent geodesic Lie groups are quasi-conformally homeomorphic, then they are quasi-isometrically equivalent. We also give more general results beyond the nilpotent case. In particular, we show that quasi-conformal homeomorphisms between geodesic Lie groups are quasi-isometries whenever the spaces have strict parabolic or hyperbolic conformal type. As a consequence, quasi-conformal homeomorphisms between geodesic Lie groups with infinite fundamental group are quasi-isometries. The statements for Lie groups are deduced from a more general study on metric measure spaces with uniformly locally bounded geometry.
item.dc:creator: Katrin F\"assler, Enrico Le Donne, Sebastiano Nicolussi Golo, Alessandro Ottazzi, Pierre Pansu

item.title: The point-cross dimension
item.description: arXiv:2607.08612v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two transverse segments have local Hausdorff and upper box dimension one at their crossing, although they carry two independent tangent directions. We define the Point-Cross Dimension by assigning each tangent line the largest local upper box dimension captured by intersection with a regular \(C^1\) curve in that direction, then taking the supremum of their sums over finite independent families of tangent lines. Every Bouligand direction admits such a recurrent curve. The resulting profile is invariant under closure and covariant under local \(C^1\)-diffeomorphisms. Each directional weight is attained, and the profile is upper semicontinuous. An integral representation by ranks of weight superlevel sets gives submodularity and, together with projection bounds, exact Cartesian-product additivity. Germs with the same projective tangent support, local upper box dimension, and rank of segment directions can have different Point-Cross Dimensions. Further computations give exact directional profiles for chirps and the Point-Cross Dimension of a self-affine carpet. Finally, approximation of a ray with error \(O(t^d)\), for \(d>1\), forces directional weight at least \(1-1/d\), and this bound is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Nadir Maaroufi

item.title: On two counterexamples in the geometry of numbers
item.description: arXiv:2607.11695v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give counterexamples to two optimization problems in dimensions eight and nine. 1. The Cartesian-product problem posed by Cassels for critical determinants and later formulated by Zong for lattice packings and for packings allowing translations but not rotations: whether the corresponding product inequalities are always equalities. The counterexample also disproves the natural product formula for unrestricted congruent packings. 2. A question raised by Sarnak and formulated as a conjecture in Chiu: whether, among unit-volume flat tori, height is minimized by a lattice maximizing the length of its shortest nonzero vector.
item.dc:creator: Nihar Gargava

item.title: On a Brunn-Minkowski principle for first-order information functionals
item.description: arXiv:2609.07463v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work we present the following general principle: every positive homogeneous functional on an abstract convex cone satisfying a suitable Brunn-Minkowski inequality gives rise to an information functional -defined as the quotient of the functional by its relative surface area- that satisfies a linear Brunn-Minkowski inequality. We also establish the dual counterpart of this principle for functionals satisfying an analogous convexity property, yielding reverse linear Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for the associated information functionals. Furthermore, we show that homogeneity is necessary within this principle by providing a counterexample to the expected result for the information functional associated to the standard Gaussian measure. As applications, we recover, via an alternative first-order argument, a classical result by Giannopoulos, Hartzoulaki and Paouris (2002) for the ratio of two consecutive quermassintegrals, together with a characterization of the equality case. The same argument extends to the setting of mixed discriminants of symmetric positive definite matrices. Finally, our approach yields new extensions of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality of Dembo, Cover and Thomas, for the classical information functional, both to the $L_p$ setting ($p \geq 1$), where the relative surface area is expressed in terms of Lutwak's first $L_p$ quermassintegral, and to the measure-theoretic framework, for measures with homogeneous densities satisfying some concavity. Moreover, we prove that our principle applies also in the context of the Blaschke addition, both in the volume and in the (mixed) affine surface area cases, obtaining new inequalities as an application of it.
item.dc:creator: Lidia Gordo Malag\'on, Eugenia Saor\'in G\'omez, Jes\'us Yepes Nicol\'as

item.title: Sobolev inequalities for sections and projections of log-concave functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32886v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Higher order sharp Sobolev and local Sobolev type inequalities for log-concave functions are established. The new inequalities directly imply the isoperimetric inequalities by Bollob\'as and Thomason in 1995, by Liakopoulos in 2019, and the recently discovered local isoperimetric inequalities from [1]. In order to do so, we make use of three ingredients. First, sets of functional inequalities proven by Alonso-Guti\'errez, Bernu\'es, Brazitikos and Carbery in 2021. Second, a multidimensional polynomial optimization result that originated in [1] and was initiated by Bollob\'as and Thomason. Third, a new integral formula for the projection of a log-concave function that links the geometric part with the more functional versions via some dependence on the Hessian matrix restricted to subspaces.
item.dc:creator: Luis J. Al\'ias, Bernardo Gonz\'alez Merino, Beatriz Mar\'in Gimeno

item.title: Coarse embeddability, $L^1$-compression and Percolations on General Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2406.04222v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that a locally finite, connected graph has a coarse embedding into a Hilbert space if and only if there exist bond percolations with arbitrarily large marginals and two-point function vanishing at infinity. We further show that the decay of the two-point function is stretched exponential with stretching exponent $\alpha\in[0,1]$ if and only if the $L^1$-compression exponent of the graph is at least $\alpha$, leading to a probabilistic characterization of this exponent. These results are new even in the particular setting of Cayley graphs of finitely generated groups. The proofs build on new probabilistic methods introduced recently by the authors to study group-invariant percolation on Cayley graphs [28,29], which are now extended to the general, non-symmetric situation of graphs to study their coarse embeddability and $L^1$-compression exponents.
item.dc:creator: Chiranjib Mukherjee, Konstantin Recke

item.title: Categorical Tiling Theory: Constructing Directed Planar Tilings via Edge Reversal
item.description: arXiv:2509.06363v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Tilings of the plane resemble the simplicial and other complexes from algebraic topology, but have not been studied from this perspective. We construct finite categories corresponding to polygons with labeled directed edges, and introduce the problem of modeling tilings of the Euclidean or hyperbolic plane as presheaves over such a category. Combinatorially, this amounts to choosing an ``alignment'' for a tiling: a direction for every edge and consistent labels for the edges of each polygonal tile. We show that for a fixed tiling, given a single alignment we can characterize every other alignment of the same tiling by comparison of the edge directions. We then construct a ``reflective'' alignment for any tiling with an even number of polygons at each vertex, and from this generate a large family of alignments with elegant symmetry properties.
item.dc:creator: Catherine DiLeo, Preston Sessoms, Brandon T. Shapiro

item.title: Magic Gems: Convex Hulls of Lifted Magic Squares
item.description: arXiv:2512.09170v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given an arrangement of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ in an $n\times n$ grid, we lift each cell to $\mathbb{R}^3$ by centring its grid coordinates $(x,y)$ at the origin and taking its centred entry $z = s_{ij} - (n^2+1)/2$ as a vertical height. The convex hull of these $n^2$ points is the gem of the arrangement, whose lower and upper boundaries are the regular subdivisions of the grid induced by $\pm z$. While random arrangements and generic linear magic squares have gems whose vertex counts grow with $n$, our main theorem shows that the classical Siamese (de la Loub\`ere) magic square of every odd order $n\ge5$ has $f$-vector $(12,26,16)$, isometry group $\{\pm\mathrm{id}\}$, and only the twelve vertices forced by the boundary of the grid. The proof shears the lift onto five horizontal terraces and reduces the hull calculation to a finite table of polynomials in $m=(n-1)/2$; the same method gives $f$-vector $(12,24,14)$ for the base-$n$ digit-exchanged square. Along any family of linear squares with fixed steps the $f$-vector is eventually periodic in $n$, whereas over all linear magic squares of prime order $n$ the maximum vertex count grows as $\Theta(\ln n)$. Whenever the heights have vanishing first moments, a short principal-axes argument shows that the point set has a non-trivial isometry if and only if the arrangement is self-complementary up to dihedral symmetry. An exact census of the $880$ magic squares of order four yields $616$ congruence classes and $352$ combinatorial types of gems, and shows that while vertex and facet counts are nearly insensitive to the magic line-sum conditions, the volume and solid centroid shift systematically.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Elliott Mathewson

item.title: Gel'fand's inverse problem under Ricci curvature bounds
item.description: arXiv:2602.14527v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The classical Gel'fand's inverse problem asks whether a Riemannian manifold is uniquely determined by the knowledge of the heat kernel on any open subset of the manifold. We study this inverse problem in the non-smooth setting in the framework of ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces, namely, metric-measure spaces with synthetic Riemannian Ricci curvature bounded below by $K$ and dimension bounded above by $N$. We establish the unique solvability of Gel'fand's inverse problem for the class of compact ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ spaces whose regular set admits Lipschitz Riemannian structure. As an application, we obtain the continuity of Gel'fand's inverse problem in the class of closed Riemannian manifolds with bounded Ricci curvature, diameter and volume bounded from below. We note that the results are new even for Einstein orbifolds and (weighted) Lipschitz Riemannian manifolds with non-smooth boundary.
item.dc:creator: Shouhei Honda, Jinpeng Lu

item.title: Area and antipodal distance in convex hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2604.02667v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a lower bound for the surface area of a closed, convex hypersurface in Euclidean space in terms of its displacement under continuous maps. As a result, a hypothesized lower bound for the volume of a Riemannian $n$-sphere, proved by Berger in dimension $n=2$ and disproved by Croke in dimensions $n \geq 3$, is valid for convex hypersurfaces in all dimensions. We also establish a sharp lower bound for the mean width of a convex hypersurface.
item.dc:creator: James Dibble, Joseph Ansel Hoisington

item.title: A groupoid approach to the equivariant coarse Baum--Connes conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2604.25595v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we develop a groupoid approach to the equivariant coarse Baum--Connes conjecture. For a bounded geometry metric space $X$ equipped with a proper, free, and isometric action of a countable discrete group $\Gamma$, we introduce the equivariant coarse groupoid $G(X, \Gamma)$. We prove that the groupoid Baum--Connes conjecture for $G(X, \Gamma)$ with coefficients in $\ell^{\infty}(X,\K)^\Ga$ is equivalent to the equivariant coarse Baum--Connes conjecture for $(X, \Gamma)$ using a localization algebra description of groupoid equivariant $KK$-theory on the Rips complex models. As applications of this framework, we prove that if the space $X$ admits a coarse embedding into Hilbert space (which is not required to be $\Gamma$-equivariant), then the equivariant coarse Novikov conjecture holds for $(X, \Gamma)$, i.e., the assembly map $\mu_{X,\Ga}$ is an injection. We also obtain a new proof of the equivariant coarse Baum--Connes conjecture if $X$ admits an equivariant coarse embedding into Hilbert space.
item.dc:creator: Liang Guo

item.title: From branching quasiflats to flats in CAT(0) cube complexes
item.description: arXiv:2605.10248v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study quasiisometric embeddings between finite-dimensional CAT(0) cube complexes. More specifically, we introduce geometric branching conditions under which flats in the domain, not necessarily of top rank, are mapped within finite Hausdorff distance of flats. As a consequence, one obtains embeddings between natural graphs associated with the Tits boundaries of those cube complexes. These results form a key step in understanding quasiisometric embeddings between right-angled Artin groups. In an appendix, we also explain how the same methods recover previously established rigidity results for quasiisometric embeddings of symmetric spaces and Euclidean buildings of the same spherical type.

item.title: Quasiisometric embeddings between right-angled Artin groups: flexibility
item.description: arXiv:2605.13314v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a complete characterisation of when the right-angled Artin group on one cycle graph can be quasiisometrically embedded in the right-angled Artin group on another cycle graph. In particular, we find infinitely many instances of quasiisometric embeddings where there is no subgroup relation. This contrasts with the fact that such groups are quasiisometrically rigid. More generally, we construct quasiisometric embeddings between graph products of finite or cyclic groups whose underlying graphs are cycles. As a special case, we obtain exotic quasiisometric embeddings of the hyperbolic plane in all right-angled Artin groups whose defining graph contains an induced cycle of length greater than four.
item.dc:creator: Shaked Bader, Oussama Bensaid, Harry Petyt

item.title: On colorful Helly numbers and the growth of Tverberg numbers
item.description: arXiv:2608.06437v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish new bounds on colorful Helly and Tverberg numbers in abstract convexity spaces with Radon number $r$. We show that the colorful Helly number is at most $(r-1)2^r$, improving Holmsen--Lee's bound $r^{r^{O(\log r)}}$ and matching the known lower bound $2^{r-1}-1$ up to a factor $O(r)$. Furthermore, we prove that the Tverberg number is $r_k=O(r^{\lceil \log_2 r\rceil }k)$, reducing P\'alv\"olgyi's coefficient $r^{r^{r^{O(\log r)}}}$ to a quasipolynomial function of $r$. For $S_4$-separable spaces, we prove $r_k=O(r^2k)$. In the other direction, we construct a sequence of $S_4$-separable spaces with Tverberg number $r_k=\Omega(r^2k)$. This shows that the weak Eckhoff conjecture, asserting that $r_k=O(rk)$ in any abstract convexity space, fails already in separable spaces. The same construction refutes the analogue of Reay's conjecture in separable spaces.
item.dc:creator: Chaya Keller, Skand Parvatikar, Tuan Tran

item.title: On the real-rootedness of Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of $(132,213)$-avoiding permutahedra
item.description: arXiv:2609.06096v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $P_d$ be the convex hull of the permutations of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ that avoid the patterns $132$ and $213$, and let $H_d(t)$ be its Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomial. We prove that all zeros of $H_d(t)$ are real and negative for $3\le d\le1000$ and for every $d\ge2^{62}$; for $d\le2$ the polynomial is constant. Expanding $H_d(t)$ in refined Eulerian polynomials does not suffice, since a coordinate is already negative at $d=7$. Let $A_{d,i}(t)$ enumerate all permutations of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with first entry $i$ by number of descents. For $c\ge0$, we prove that every nonnegative linear combination of $A_{d,1},\ldots,A_{d,d}$ and the adjacent differences $A_{d,r+1}-cA_{d,r}$, $2\le r\le d-2$, is real-rooted for all $d\ge4$ simultaneously if and only if $c\le2-\sqrt3$. This reduces real-rootedness to the positivity of explicit weighted tails of the coordinates. An exact certificate checks these inequalities for $d\le1000$, and coefficient estimates based on Darroch's theorem on the mode of a sum of Bernoulli variables prove them for $d\ge2^{62}$; the range $1001\le d<2^{62}$ remains open. Along the way we identify $P_d$, up to lattice equivalence, with twice a chain-poset permutahedron and with the Newton polytope of a discriminant, which transfers the known cube structure and volume of these models to $P_d$. We also show that the coefficient of $t^{d-1}$ in $H_d(t)$ counts strong tournament score sequences for $d\ge3$, confirming a conjecture of Rehberg in this range.
